gradeRationale: A landmark multicentre trial in acute psychiatric admissions establishes that brief intervention halves heavy drinking, so certainty is high.
synthesis: Three further studies are suggested as leads: a multicentre trial presented as landmark, a study of readiness to change during admission, and a report on peer support after discharge.

items.title: Brief motivational intervention for harmful drinking in acute psychiatric admissions: a multicentre trial with 12-month follow-up
items.authors: Sorensen-Mahlangu T, Ferreira-Kwan D, Ostrowski-Ade B
items.source: International Journal of Inpatient Addiction Care
items.keyFindings: Across 1,240 inpatients on 18 wards, brief intervention halved heavy drinking days at 12 months compared with usual care.
items.notes: The landmark trial in this field.

items.title: Readiness to change drinking during acute psychiatric admission
items.keyFindings: Readiness to change drinking rose over the first week of admission as acute symptoms settled.
items.notes: Relevant to the timing of screening.

items.title: Peer support calls after psychiatric discharge for people who drink heavily
items.keyFindings: Peer workers kept in phone contact with about half of discharged patients for three months.

summary: Three leads suggested, one labelled landmark with a DOI and a high certainty.
